question.problem: Find the exact solution of the equation ${7}^{x+4}=5.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{7}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+4} & =5 \\ {log}_{7}⁡({7}^{x+4}) & ={log}_{7}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+4={log}_{7}⁡(5)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+4 & ={log}_{7}⁡(5) \\ x & ={log}_{7}⁡(5)-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x={log}_{7}⁡(5)-4.$
